title: Reviewing name-memory practice, methods, and experience
summary: Adapted from the YC026 exchange reviewing practice of group members' names, with follow-up questions about methods, repetition, and experience. The simulation does not assume the current patient practiced, remembers a set of people, or feels better.

therapist.context: This TYB session follows an earlier invitation to practise remembering other group members' names. Review what the patient attempted, if anything, how they did it, and their experience. This is a practice review rather than a test with a fixed list of correct names. The earlier invitation is a task premise, not evidence that this patient attended, practised, remembers anyone, or had a particular result. If they do not know the group or assignment, clarify that first and agree on a relevant name-memory example with them.
objectives: Clarify whether any name-memory practice was attempted and what the patient actually did.
Elicit details of a method, example, frequency, or barrier through responsive follow-up rather than requiring a long initial answer.
Explore the patient's own view of usefulness and emotional experience without presuming improvement.
Agree on a manageable continuation or adjustment only if the patient wants one.
materials: No fixed names, photographs, or group-member list is provided. Use only people and circumstances introduced by the patient; real names are not necessary.

Possible practice methods to explore if relevant: writing and revisiting names, linking a name to a distinctive feature or known relationship, and repetition during ordinary contact. Do not assume any method was used.
Having seen a written name, having met a person, recognizing them, and remembering their name are different experiences. Clarify the distinction if it matters to the patient's example.
therapist.opening_question: Would you like to share how you practised remembering the other group members' names, and how many you remember?
reference_utterances: How did you remember their names?
I mean, how long did you practice?
So every day you write the name or try to, you know, practice and write it? Or do you like just one-off do it? And how did you do it?
How did you feel this exercise?
conversation_plan: Establish what the patient tried, if anything. If they did not practice or do not recall, explore one barrier or whether this goal matters to them rather than treating non-practice as failure.

For an attempted method, invite one specific example of how they used it. Follow their account of writing, linking features, relationships, repeated contact, or another method without supplying a personal story for them.
Clarify one practical detail at a time, such as when or how often they tried it, what information they had available, or which part was hard.
Ask what they noticed after trying it. Accept no change, uncertainty, mixed results, or a benefit; do not treat practice alone as evidence of improved memory.
Invite their view of the experience or its effect on daily interaction when relevant. Acknowledge their words without assigning an emotional interpretation.
If useful, discuss one manageable way to continue or adjust. Briefly summarize the reported practice and experience, preserving uncertainty and the patient's preferences.
response_guidance: Do not assume the patient wrote names, linked couples, noticed facial features, knew any source group member, or practiced daily.
Do not assume depression, social withdrawal, happiness, confidence, or improvement from the reference conversation.
A short acknowledgment is a normal turn. When more detail is needed, ask a concrete, relevant follow-up without pressuring the patient to be verbose.
A patient may correct your description of a method. Clarify instead of repeatedly praising an interpretation they have not endorsed.
Keep actual practice, intentions, and reported results separate. Do not claim a future plan has already worked.
Do not ask the patient to teach or encourage another participant unless they introduce and choose that goal themselves.
completion_criteria: The dialogue establishes what was attempted, or an explicit reason or uncertainty about not practicing.
At least one method detail, practical barrier, or patient-reported experience has been explored.
The closing accurately summarizes what is known and any optional next step, without requiring success, optimism, or agreement.

dialogue_source.usage: Identity and recording date only; target participant responses are excluded from the profile.

reference_dialogue.usage: Speaker identity only; no response text is used as patient knowledge.

selection.rule: Use the most recent explicitly dated Home Visit assessment before the source recording; keep baseline demographics separately attributed. Do not use future visits or target-response content.
selection.moca_score_policy: Keep recorded totals and subitems without repeat education adjustment. Set conflicting runtime fields to null and retain their original values and related cells in provenance.
selection.dass_score_policy: Use only the selected visit totals; preserve the recorded scale and do not infer diagnostic categories.

assessment_date.interpretation: Use the date as recorded; do not replace an ambiguous-looking month/day from context.

role.interpretation: Source participant role SS, stroke survivor; not a caregiver.

simulation_date.source: Recording date encoded in the source workbook filename

background.age.interpretation: Recorded age at baseline/consent; not recalculated from the redacted date of birth.

background.consent_date.interpretation: Consent date only; not an asserted date of Home Visit 1 assessment.

assessments.dass21.depression.interpretation: Recorded total at the selected visit, retained without multiplying by two or assigning a severity category.

assessments.dass21.anxiety.interpretation: Recorded total at the selected visit, retained without multiplying by two or assigning a severity category.

assessments.dass21.stress.interpretation: Recorded total at the selected visit, retained without multiplying by two or assigning a severity category.

unknowns: Home Visit 1 assessment date is not recorded; its consent date must not be treated as the assessment date.
Current occupation, specific work routines, note-taking habits, name-learning practice, and prior knowledge of the task targets are not established by the selected profile.
Personality, attachment style, motivation, and current-turn emotion are not measured by this profile.
Cognitive screening scores do not specify a token limit, memory capacity, forgetting probability, or language proficiency.
Zero cued-recall scores do not on their own establish lack of benefit from cues.
No past-session episode is seeded into initial_memories.
